subject: Renewal: committed pool increase + throughput SLA and overflow approach
messages:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Ortiz <samantha.ortiz@bluegrid.ai>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2027 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal: committed pool increase + throughput SLA and overflow approach

Hi Samantha —

Thanks again for the renewal signal yesterday. To make the renewal discussion concrete, here’s a proposed path that addresses BlueGrid’s growth profile and procurement needs:

Summary proposal (high level)
- Term: 12 months (start: 2027-06-01)
- Reserved pool add: +8 GPUs (A100-equivalent), bringing you to a 24 GPU reserved pool
- Throughput guidance: sustained target 150 requests/sec at 512-token average (expected p95 latency under 200ms). We can formalize p99 in the SLA below.
- Burst / overflow: two options we can include in the amendment:
  1) Soft spill (preferred): automatic overflow to on-demand capacity up to 25% of committed pool during sustained events; overflow billed at on-demand rate with monthly surge credits equal to 50% of the first 100k overflow tokens each month.
  2) Hard cap: enforce a strict cap at committed capacity; customer pre-purchases burst credits (blocks of GPU-hours) to cover overflow.

Ask from BlueGrid: which of the two overflow models does procurement prefer? Procurement note: hard caps simplify billing predictability; soft spill is operationally simpler and avoids throttling.

Attached is a draft amendment showing both options in redline and a quick cost delta for each. If you’re aligned, we’ll prepare an execution-ready DocuSign with the chosen overflow model and throughput SLAs (including credit terms for missed p99).

Next steps I suggest:
- Procurement decision on overflow model by 4/22
- If soft spill: finalize surge credit amount and on-demand rates; we’ll include a 6-month promotional burst credit for the first renewal term.
- If hard cap: indicate expected monthly burst-hour purchase or target buffer.

I’m copying Aditya and Laura to align commercial terms and Marcus for sizing/ops.

Thanks —
Rachel

Rachel Kim
Head of Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Renewal: committed pool increase + throughput SLA and overflow approach

Rachel —

Thanks for the clear proposal. BlueGrid likes the idea of adding capacity but procurement flagged the soft-spill option because of variable billing. Our primary ask: predictable monthly spend. A couple of clarifying Qs: 

1) If we take soft spill with surge credits, what’s the worst-case monthly charge we should anticipate for a 25% overflow event sustained for 48 hours? Please provide a concrete example (numbers).
2) For the hard cap option, what are the minimum burst-credit blocks and can those credits be used across multiple regions?
3) We require explicit throughput guarantees in the amendment (p99) or an agreed credit formula tied to observed throughput degradation.

Procurement requests the legal PO to proceed once we agree on billing. I’m including our procurement alias.

—Samantha
Samantha Ortiz
Head of Platform Engineering, BlueGrid.ai
samantha.ortiz@bluegrid.ai

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Renewal: committed pool increase + throughput SLA and overflow approach

Quick internal plan for negotiation and numbers to send back to BlueGrid: 

Commercial offer (recommended)
- Term: 12 months start 2027-06-01
- Add 8 GPUs reserved (24 total) — list price delta: $64,000/mo at standard committed rate.
- Discount: 15% on the incremental reserved capacity for 12-month commit -> net incremental $54,400/mo.
- Burst handling (preferred combo): soft spill up to 25% with on-demand rate = $0.70 / GPU-hour equivalent; include 100k surge-credit tokens per month (valued at ~$6,000/mo) complimentary for first 6 months.
- Hard cap alternative: offer pre-purchasable burst credits in 100 GPU-hour blocks ($80 / GPU-hour) with a 10% volume discount for upfront purchase of >= 500 GPU-hours.
- SLA: p99 latency credit: if p99 > 350ms for two consecutive weeks, apply 5% credit to monthly invoice per affected route; if > 600ms then 15% credit.

Ask from sales: are we comfortable with the on-demand rate above for the soft-spill public sheet? Also need ops to confirm sustained throughput estimate and whether we should tighten p99 thresholds. Marcus — can you confirm that 150 req/sec sustained at 512 tokens is feasible with the 24 GPU pool and soft-spill behaviour?

I’ve attached an edited amendment (redlines + pricing table) for Rachel to send.

-Aditya

Thanks, Aditya and Rachel — that helps. A few items before we route to our CFO for sign-off: 

- The example numbers for soft spill worst-case would be helpful. Please include a worked example showing cost delta for a 48-hour 25% overflow event (we need to budget).
- We require the SLA credit to reference the monitoring window and measurement method (Redwood's per-route p99 over 7-day rolling window). Please add that text in the amendment.
- SOC2 attestation: please include a link to the SOC2 report and confirm SOC2 Type II coverage includes the Dedicated control plane.
- DocuSign: once legal confirms the amendment language we’ll sign via DocuSign. Please include DocuSign link in the execution package.

I’ve attached our PO to accelerate finance sign-off once the amendment is in order.

Thanks —
Samantha

Samantha —

Appreciate the quick turn. Actions and next steps from our side: 

1) Worked example: Aditya will include a 48-hour 25% overflow worked example and line-item cost delta in the execution package by 4/30.
2) Amendment updates: we will add explicit monitoring language — Redwood per-route p99 measured over a 7-day rolling window (prometheus + tracing) and the credit triggers you requested.
3) SOC2: confirm link to published SOC2 Type II report is included in the package (see link below). The Dedicated control plane is covered per our attestation scope.
4) DocuSign: we’ll generate a DocuSign envelope containing the finalized amendment + your PO and route to your CFO. Expect the DocuSign link in the email thread on 5/1.

Proposed timeline: finalize commercial terms and amendment text by 4/30 -> DocuSign 5/1 -> target execution 5/5 to align with provisioning so the new GPUs are ready by 6/1.

If procurement prefers the hard-cap option, let us know and we’ll include burst credit pricing instead of surge credits.

Thanks — looking forward to closing this out.
